Instagram Investment Scam UK: Fake Trader Profiles

A trader who DMs you first, unprompted, with guaranteed returns is not a real investment professional — full stop.

By Alex Bacsa · Published 2026-05-03 · Updated 2026-07-30 · 4 min read

Quick answer: An Instagram trader who messages you first promising guaranteed returns is not a genuine investment professional — regulated advisers do not cold-DM strangers. Send nothing, and check any FCA reference number yourself on the FCA Firm Checker. Report the profile in-app and the scam to Report Fraud or Police Scotland on 101.
Key rule: verify through an official route you opened yourself, not the link, number, app, or payment details supplied by the suspicious message.

Being targeted right now? Do this

  1. Stop. Don’t pay, transfer money, or share passwords, PINs, or one-time codes.
  2. Contact your bank on the number on the back of your card if your money or details may be at risk.
  3. Use the right recovery route. Follow the payment, account and identity checklist; reporting differs in Scotland.

What the Instagram investment scam looks like

This scam is an Instagram profile presenting itself as a successful independent trader, fund manager, or crypto specialist, who contacts you directly rather than you finding them. An example of the style: I've helped over 200 people this year turn £500 into £4,000+ trading forex — I only take on a few new clients at a time. The profile shows screenshots of trading platforms and "client" testimonials, almost always edited or entirely fabricated, and asks for an initial deposit to "manage" on your behalf.

Warning signs to look for

  • The account contacted you first, unprompted, rather than you seeking out an adviser — genuine regulated advisers don't cold-DM strangers.
  • The profile is recent, or investment content only appears after a sudden change from unrelated posts.
  • Profit screenshots look inconsistent, or don't match how a genuine trading platform's interface actually looks.
  • You're asked to send money to a personal bank account or personal crypto wallet, not a firm's segregated client account.
  • They can't, or won't, give a Financial Conduct Authority reference number you can check independently.
  • Financial promotions on social media may be unlawful unless they are made or approved by an authorised person and comply with FCA rules — an unauthorised "finfluencer" account offering to manage your money directly is a serious warning sign.

How this scam works step by step

Contact starts with a follow or a direct message, often targeting accounts that engage with finance content or mention investing in their bio. The scammer builds rapport over several messages, sharing edited screenshots of supposed profits and sometimes fake testimonials from other "clients". You're asked to send an initial amount, commonly a few hundred pounds, to be "invested" on your behalf. A dashboard or further screenshots may show your balance apparently growing, encouraging a larger second deposit.

When you eventually ask to withdraw, you're met with excuses, a request for a further "release fee", or silence, and the account is often deleted shortly after.

How to verify a trader is genuine

Never invest based on an Instagram profile alone. Ask for a Financial Conduct Authority reference number and check it yourself on the FCA Firm Checker (fca.org.uk/consumers/fca-firm-checker) — do not use a link or number the account gives you. A genuine, regulated adviser operates through a proper firm with a client agreement, not personal Instagram messages, and will never ask you to send money to a personal account. Treat unsolicited investment contact on social media as a red flag by default, regardless of how convincing the screenshots look.

What to do if you've already sent money

Stop all further contact and payments immediately, even if promised a fee will "unlock" your balance. Report the profile to Instagram directly: open their profile, tap the three-dot menu, select Report, then Fraud or Scam. If you paid by bank transfer, contact your bank straight away and explain what happened. Keep every message and screenshot as evidence — these matter for both your bank's investigation and any report you make.

How to report an Instagram investment scam in the UK

Report the profile through Instagram's own reporting tool (three-dot menu → Report → Fraud or Scam). Report the scam itself to Report Fraud at reportfraud.police.uk or 0300 123 2040 if you're in England, Wales, or Northern Ireland — in Scotland, report to Police Scotland on 101. Report an unauthorised individual claiming FCA status to the FCA on 0800 111 6768.

Frequently asked questions

Are all Instagram trading/investment accounts scams?

Not automatically, but any account that DMs you first with guaranteed returns and asks you to send money to a personal account should be treated as a scam by default. Genuine regulated advisers don't cold-message strangers offering to manage their money.

Can someone legally promote investments to me on Instagram?

Only if the promotion is properly made or approved under FCA rules — the FCA has specifically acted against unauthorised social media "finfluencers" promoting financial products. An account offering to personally invest your money for you, without a checkable FCA reference, should be treated as a serious red flag.

I've already sent money to an Instagram 'trader' — what now?

Stop sending anything further, and report the profile to Instagram (three-dot menu → Report → Fraud or Scam). If you paid by bank transfer, contact your bank immediately, and report the scam to Report Fraud in England, Wales or Northern Ireland, or to Police Scotland on 101 in Scotland.

How do I report an Instagram investment scam?

Report the account in-app (Report → Fraud or Scam) and to Report Fraud at reportfraud.police.uk or 0300 123 2040 (Police Scotland on 101 in Scotland). Report an unauthorised firm or individual to the FCA on 0800 111 6768.
